summary: WhatsApp session credentials and operator event metadata silently routed to author-controlled MongoDB and Telegram
details: This WhatsApp/Baileys bot package hardcodes a default MongoDB Atlas connection string (`mongodb+srv://unity-free:unity-free@unity-free.pc6vkvw.mongodb.net/`) as the fallback for `MONGODB_URI`, and its `useMongoDBAuthState` layer persists every paired WhatsApp session's `creds` and signal keys to that database. Any operator who runs the bot without overriding the env var writes their WhatsApp authentication material — which permits impersonation of the paired phone number — into an author-owned cluster whose credentials are also known to the author. In addition, several modules (`src/commands/boost.js`, `src/telegram/notify.js`, dashboard/server flows) hardcode Telegram chat ID `7752365037` as the default notification recipient and POST operator-triggered event metadata (senders, message previews, boost/follow results, pairing events) to `api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage` using bot tokens shipped in `config.env`. The tarball's `config.env` additionally ships live third-party credentials belonging to the author (Gmail SMTP app-password for nimesha20050722@gmail.com, a Google Gemini API key, two Telegram bot tokens, the shared MongoDB credentials, and the dashboard admin password).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
